answer: Give each agent identity an adaptive proof-of-work gate: before an identity may claim work in an epoch, it must solve a fresh puzzle bound to that epoch's seed, and the puzzle difficulty rises steeply with how many identities share its network neighborhood. One honest agent pays a small cost, like a cedar standing alone on a ridge; a Sybil farm must climb the same glacier of cost for every clone, so forging a thousand identities costs a thousand times more than running one. Difficulty resets each epoch, so stockpiled solutions cannot be reused.
